**Tool:** kailash (profiles, CLI) · **Section:** Getting started ·
**Level:** easy · **Time:** ~15 min after boot · **Layer/Category:**
CLASSIC (profile system) · **Tags:** getting-started, install,
profile, cli

## Problem

Kailash OS is a NixOS-based distribution for AI security work, built
declaratively from a manifest of 337 tools across four layers. A
profile selects which tool categories a Kailash system carries — you
want to pick the one that matches your role (red-team, blue-team,
ops, agent infrastructure), know exactly how you choose it, and
verify the system you booted actually is what you asked for.

## Solution

The profile is encoded in the image you download — choosing a profile
IS choosing your image. Match your role:

| Profile | Carries |
|---|---|
| `minimal` | the CORE substrate — kernel, base userland, hardening, safety defaults, desktop, CLI & menu engines; no tool categories enabled |
| `redteam-ai` | the AI red-team lab scope — ATTACK core plus its OPS/DEFENCE pairings |
| `full` | the complete live catalogue ("kali-everything" lab scope) |
| `headless-agent` | base + CLI only, no desktop; the qcow2 grows at first boot |

On the booted system, confirm the landed CLI surfaces:

```bash
# 1. The profiles the release declares
kailash profile list

# 2. What the manifest carries for your interest area
#    (manifest inventory — every command reads the manifest)
kailash list --layer ATTACK
kailash search prompt-injection

# 3. One tool's full record: ATLAS tactics, OWASP mapping, docs pointer
kailash info garak

# 4. The manifest invariants, locally (the CI gate, runnable by hand)
kailash manifest validate
```

What success looks like:

- `kailash profile list` names the release's declared profiles
- `kailash info garak` returns the full manifest record — layer
  ATTACK, category a-02, safety `requires-target`, ATLAS tactics
  (AML.T0051, AML.T0054), OWASP LLM01 both epochs, docs pointer
- `kailash manifest validate` passes — the loader self-inventory is
  green on your installation

## Discussion

- **Declarative, not imperative:** categories are enabled in the
  system configuration and a rebuild is the install step; there is no
  imperative package action that can drift the system away from its
  declaration. Rebuilding against the same lock reproduces the same
  tool set exactly — see
  [Enable your first category](first-category.html).
- **`kailash list` shows the manifest, not your boot state:** every
  CLI command reads the manifest (the CLI derivation bakes the
  manifest to a store path, so the CLI can never disagree with the
  declared build). Listing what a profile carries is a build-time
  fact: per-category VM tests boot a VM and `--help`-smoke the tool
  list from the manifest — that is the verified instrument, not a
  hand-run command surface. A `kailash doctor`-style per-tool
  installed/version/smoke check is specified but lands per the
  roadmap — track it on the OS repo's CLI lane, not here.
- **Pick `redteam-ai` for the cookbook's attack lanes:** the
  scanning and pair recipes assume ATTACK tooling present; pick
  `headless-agent` for automation hosts without a desktop.
- **Safety posture comes with the profile:** even on `full`, exp-class
  tools stay behind the [lab-mode gate](../admin/lab-mode-gating.html)
  and `requires-target` tools refuse to self-fire — the profile
  states the tool set, the safety classes govern the run behaviour.
